methods.name: Create
methods.description:
Create a plan.

 The plan's slug is its stable handle and must be unique across the
 catalog. The spec is final at create: to change any term, create a new
 Plan and retire this one.

methods.name: Retire
methods.description:
Retire a plan so it can no longer be bought.

 Existing subscriptions and licenses on the plan keep it; the plan stays
 readable so they can show their terms. Retiring an already retired plan
 changes nothing.

methods.name: Get
methods.description:
Get a plan by its unique identifier.

 Any signed-in caller may read any plan, retired plans included.

methods.name: List
methods.description:
List the plans in the catalog.

 Returns the active plans; set include_retired to see retired ones too.
 Any signed-in caller may list.

methodTypes.name: ListPlansInput
methodTypes.description: ListPlansInput selects which plans to list.

fields.name: IncludeRetired
fields.description:
When true, retired plans are included beside the active ones; by
 default only plans that can still be bought are returned.

methodTypes.name: Plans
methodTypes.description: Plans contains a list of plan resources.

enumTypes.name: PlanLifecycle
enumTypes.description:
PlanLifecycle is whether a plan can still be bought.

 A retired plan stays readable so a subscription or license that bought it
 can still show its terms; retirement is the only state change a plan has.

values.name: retired
values.description: No longer offered; existing subscriptions and licenses keep it.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines which
 users, inside that organization or in its child organizations, can read
 the resource. No level reaches every
 account on the server.

 The visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer tuple (everyone in the
   org — the org role hierarchy flows downward, so owners, admins, members
   AND read-only viewers all satisfy the organization#viewer userset)
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer
   (everyone in every child organization of the owning organization)
 - PUBLIC: retired; see the value's own comment.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner, explicitly granted principals, and — for blueprint kinds
 in the cloud edition — org admins can access.
 This is the default for personal and run-scoped resources.

 Org admins count as owners of blueprint kinds (agent, agent_share,
 skill, plugin), so a private blueprint stays
 manageable — and visible — to its org's admins. Personal kinds
 (sessions) stay creator-only.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Retired. This level made a resource readable to every account on the
 server; it is refused at create and at updateVisibility for every kind,
 and every stored row that held it has been moved to visibility_org.
 Sharing across organizations happens through plugins (a copy is
 installed and owned) or, from a parent organization to its children,
 through visibility_child_orgs.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
Everyone in the owning organization can access (read) this resource —
 all org roles including read-only viewers (the role SSO auto-provisioning
 grants by default). Running or otherwise spending against the resource
 still requires the org-level member-or-guest permissions
 (can_create_session / can_create_run_in); org visibility widens
 read, never spend.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 (The tuple once targeted organization#member, which
 excluded viewer-role users; the authorization model no longer admits
 that shape.)

values.name: visibility_child_orgs
values.description:
Everyone in every child organization of the owning organization can
 read and run this resource: the shared catalog an organization offers
 the organizations under it (spec.parent_org). Child organizations
 created later gain access automatically, and no other organization
 does. Instances, sessions, runs and vaults are never shared
 this way: each child runs the shared blueprint inside its own boundary.

 Only valid for blueprint kinds with supports_child_orgs: true, and only
 in an organization that is not itself a child.

 FGA tuple: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

enumTypes.name: PlanInstrument
enumTypes.description:
The instrument a plan is bought through.

 An entitlement is what the platform permits; a subscription and a license
 are the two instruments that grant it. A plan names which one buys it, so
 the catalog for Stigmer Cloud and the catalog for self-hosted licenses are
 two views of one kind.

values.name: subscription
values.description:
Bought as a Subscription by an organization on Stigmer Cloud, billed
 monthly against usage.

values.name: license
values.description: Bought as a License by a self-hosting customer, invoiced for a term.

enumTypes.name: Feature
enumTypes.description:
A capability an entitlement can unlock.

 The vocabulary is closed and grows one value at a time, each landing with
 the gate that reads it: an enum value is a wire identifier that can never
 be removed, so a feature is named here only once something in the
 platform can be gated on it. Values are added, never renamed or reused.

values.name: sso_enforcement
values.description:
Enforcing sign-in through a registered identity provider, so members
 cannot use another login. The identity-provider kind is Enterprise and
 Cloud; this feature is what a plan or license turns on for it.

values.name: platform_client
values.description:
Gates nothing: every edition serves PlatformClient credentials to every
 customer, so a plan or license that lists it grants nothing more.
 It is the one value named before its gate was ruled out, and it stays
 because licenses already issued carry it and an enum value is a wire
 identifier. A new plan or license does not list it.

values.name: byo_provider_keys
values.description:
Bringing the customer's own LLM provider keys instead of the platform's
 metered proxy credentials.

values.name: channels
values.description:
Delivering agents over messaging channels (Slack, WhatsApp) through a
 channel runtime. The channel kinds themselves are open source; this
 feature tiers the Cloud's hosted runtime inside Cloud plans. It is not
 an edition gate, and a license never lists it: the open-source server
 stores channels freely, and whether a self-hosted server delivers them
 is its edition's to decide, never its license's.

values.name: sharing
values.description:
Sharing an agent through hosted share links, with the sharing
 organization's members or with anyone who has the link. The agent-share
 kind itself is open source; this feature tiers the Cloud's hosted
 sharing lane inside Cloud plans. It is not an edition gate, and a
 license never lists it: the open-source server stores shares freely,
 and whether a self-hosted server serves its links to guests is its
 edition's to decide, never its license's.

values.name: teams
values.description:
Creating teams and adding members to them. The team kind is Enterprise
 and Cloud; this feature tiers it inside Cloud plans, so an organization
 on a plan without it keeps its existing teams but cannot create one or
 add a member. It is not an edition gate: an Enterprise deployment
 includes teams by the kind's tier, and a license never lists it.

values.name: child_orgs
values.description:
Creating child organizations (spec.parent_org), the organizations an
 integrator runs for its own customers. A plan lists it together with
 included_child_orgs: the feature admits new child organizations, and
 the limit is how many the plan includes before the per-organization
 fee. Without it, existing children keep working and no new one is
 admitted. It tiers the Cloud runtime and is not an edition gate; a
 license never lists it.

resourceDescription:
Plan is a catalog entry naming a bundle of entitlements and the terms that
 buy it.

 A plan is bought through one of two instruments: a Subscription (an
 organization on Stigmer Cloud) or a License (a self-hosting customer). The
 entitlements it names are the platform's vocabulary; the terms are the
 cloud's. A plan is immutable once created: a change of terms is a new Plan,
 and the old one retires so existing subscriptions can still show what they
 bought. Plans belong to the platform, not to any organization, so
 metadata.org is empty. No plan ships in the contract; the catalog's rows
 are seeded by the cloud.

statusType.name: PlanStatus
statusType.description:
PlanStatus is the system-managed state of a plan: its audit trail and
 whether it is still offered.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description: Standard audit information tracking creation and modification.

fields.name: Lifecycle
fields.description: Whether the plan is offered to new buyers or retired.

fields.name: RetiredAt
fields.description: When the plan was retired. Unset while the plan is active.

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAudit
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAudit contains both spec-level and status-level audit details.

fields.name: SpecAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's specification (desired state).

fields.name: StatusAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's status (actual state).

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAuditActor
statusNestedTypes.description:
ApiResourceAuditActor represents the entity that performed an action.

 This is the platform's single actor vocabulary: every "who did this"
 reference (created_by / updated_by, version-history applied_by / pushed_by,
 approval resolved_by_actor) uses this message, so actor rendering is
 uniform across all surfaces.

fields.name: Avatar
fields.description: URL to the actor's avatar image.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.description:
Human-readable display name (e.g. "Ada Lovelace"). Empty when unknown;
 renderers fall back to email, then id.

fields.name: Email
fields.description:
Email address of the actor. Empty when unknown or not applicable
 (e.g. machine accounts).

fields.name: PlatformClientId
fields.description:
The PlatformClient whose minted user token the actor acted through.
 Empty for every other credential, and on an actor that records no act
 (an account's profile lookup).

fields.name: CreatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was created.

fields.name: UpdatedBy
fields.description: Actor who last updated this resource.

fields.name: UpdatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was last updated.
